architecture.approach: Widen the v1 seams rather than add layers. The `mail/` module already resolves its transport through the `MAIL_SERVICE` provider token, so an SMTP transport (nodemailer, configured for Mailtrap from environment variables) is dropped in behind that token while `ConsoleMailService` stays for local and test. Invitation state becomes a first-class column: an `InvitationStatus` enum (PENDING, ACCEPTED, REJECTED, CANCELLED) is persisted on `invitations`, a `DeliveryStatus` (PENDING, SENT, FAILED) plus `deliveryError` records the mail outcome, and `EXPIRED` is derived at read time for an unconsumed row whose `expiresAt` has passed - never written - so no scheduler is needed. Cancel, decline, resend and role change are new tenant-scoped operations in the existing `tenancy` module, gated by the shared `CAPABILITY_ROLES` matrix and audited through the existing transactional `AuditService`. The invitation link gains `organizationId`, `clinicId` and `role` as conveniences, but the persisted invitation row stays the single source of truth: the server always re-derives the join scope from the record and ignores the link claims (FR-047). The mail send runs outside the invitation transaction (NFR-016) and its outcome is recorded, so a provider failure degrades to a resend affordance rather than a lost invitation.

dataModel.flowDescription: An admin issues an invitation: the row is written inside a transaction as PENDING with a hashed single-use token and a deliveryStatus of PENDING, the transaction commits, and only then is the email sent outside it (NFR-016). The send outcome (SENT, or FAILED with a recorded error) is written back, and a failed send still leaves the invitation PENDING with a resend affordance (EC-019). The link carries the token plus organizationId, clinicId and role as convenience claims. The accept page calls GET /api/invitations/:token, which resolves the email-known flag and the scope from the persisted record without consuming the token. On accept the server re-derives the join scope from the record, ignores any disagreeing link claim (FR-047), consumes the token and writes ACCEPTED. Cancel writes CANCELLED, decline writes REJECTED, and each invalidates the token; every mutation writes an audit row in the same transaction. A PENDING row whose expiresAt has passed is reported as EXPIRED at read time and never written.

securityConsiderations.description: SMTP credentials are read only from environment variables, never logged, and the raw invitation token is neither logged nor returned over HTTP (AC-046).
Every new mail configuration key is documented in server/.env.example by name only, with no value that works as a production default (CON-519, NFR-007).
The mail send runs outside the database transaction, so a slow or failing provider cannot hold a transaction open or roll back the invitation row.
Invitation and reset templates escape every interpolated value and never use dangerouslySetInnerHTML (NFR-005, CON-517).
The directory renders status labels in EN, AR and FR with RTL-correct layout and no hard-coded user-facing strings (CON-304, CON-305).
The invitation and member lists are paginated so a read never loads every invitation for an organization in one response.
Settings and role writes are tenant-scoped and gated by manageSettings; every write is audited with actor and before/after values.
Custom-role permissions are validated against the base role capability set, preventing privilege escalation beyond the base role.
The organization overview filters by the tenant organization and never accepts an arbitrary organization id from the client.
A workspace switch requires an active membership and issues a fresh scoped token; the client proves the refresh cookie before reload.

performanceConsiderations.strategy: The provider call is removed from the request transaction and its outcome recorded, so invitation creation stays a bounded single-transaction write regardless of provider latency.
The list endpoints take a bounded page size and use the existing (clinicId, status) and (expiresAt) indexes so a directory read is an index scan, not a full scan.
The overview is one aggregate query with per-clinic rows scoped to the organization; it does not fan out into a full record read per clinic.

dependencies.name: Mailtrap
dependencies.notes: Transactional SMTP provider for invitations and resets (BP-047); credentials supplied per environment. Not manifest-verifiable.

risks.description: Changing a member's role is a privilege-escalation path.
risks.mitigation: The endpoint is gated by CAPABILITY_ROLES, changes are tenant-scoped via clinicWhere, and every change is audited (FR-045, AC-060).

risks.description: The invitation link carries organization and clinic ids an attacker could tamper with.
risks.mitigation: The link claims are advisory only; the server resolves the persisted invitation record as the source of truth and ignores a disagreeing claim (FR-047, AC-064).

risks.description: A synchronous provider call on the request path could slow or fail invitation creation.
risks.mitigation: The send runs outside the invitation transaction (NFR-016) and a failed send is recorded, not thrown, so the row is still created and a resend is offered (AC-049, EC-019).

risks.description: Adding a non-persisted EXPIRED state could drift from the stored status.
risks.mitigation: EXPIRED is derived only at read time for a PENDING row whose expiresAt has passed, so there is a single source of truth and no scheduler (FR-042, AC-051).

risks.description: Custom roles could grant more than their base role.
risks.mitigation: The API rejects any permission outside the base role capability set (NFR-021, AC-068).

risks.description: The organization overview could leak another organization's counts.
risks.mitigation: The service filters by the resolved tenant organization and returns only that organization (FR-054, NFR-023).

risks.description: A failed workspace switch could leave a token for the rejected clinic.
risks.mitigation: The switch validates membership before issuing a token, and the client proves the refresh before reload (NFR-024, AC-073).

risks.description: Placeholder settings sections could imply backend behaviour that does not exist.
risks.mitigation: The placeholders are labelled as not yet available and make no API mutation (FR-052, AC-069).
